subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for November 25, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Prehospital Fluid Resuscitation for Patients With Suspected Se
sentences: Story 1 is about Prehospital Fluid Resuscitation for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: The PITSTOP-Fluids Factorial Randomized Clinical Trial..
This is a randomized / clinical trial from JAMA.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in Participants were adults with suspected sepsis, defined as suspected infection, fever (≥38, how should we interpret l fluid resuscitation strategy for the prehospital management of patients with suspected sepsis did not reduce mortality compared with more restrictive usual care. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03068741?
The median age of patients was 76 (IQR, 63-85) years and 938 (57.0%) were male.

Most patients in both groups received a fluid bolus (826/848 [97.4%] in the liberal fluids group; 700/821 [85.3%] in the usual fluids group) during transport, but patients in the liberal fluids group received a larger volume (median, 1500 mL [IQR, 1000-2000 mL]) vs 500 mL [IQR, 175-800 mL] in the usual fluids group; difference, 910.1 mL [95% CI, 857.3-962.9 mL]).

Hospital mortality was 149/830 (18.0%) in the liberal fluids group and 149/816 (18.3%) in the usual fluids group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.80-1.20]; unadjusted risk difference, -0.3 [95% CI, -4.0 to 3.4]; P = .82).

To determine the effect of earlier treatment with antibiotics in the ambulance on 90-day mortality compared with usual treatment in the emergency department. The median (IQR) age of patients was 75 (62-85) years and 1162 (56.7%) were males.

Most patients (735 of 795 [92.5%] in the ceftriaxone group and 730 of 792 [92.2%] in placebo group) were treated with antibiotics in the hospital after a mean (SD) of 247.3 (207.7) minutes after paramedic arrival among patients in the ceftriaxone group and 252.8 (218.0) minutes among the placebo group.

script.heading: Story 3 - Association of preoperative vaping-related disorder versus cig
sentences: Story 3 is about Association of preoperative vaping-related disorder versus cigarette nicotine dependence with postoperative respiratory complications: a multicentre matched cohort study..
This is a cohort study from British journal of anaesthesia.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in patients with documented preoperative vaping-related disorder and cigarette nicotine dependence, how should we interpret Association of preoperative vaping-related disorder compared with cigarette nicotine dependence with postoperative respiratory complications: a multicentre matched cohort study?

Among 3817 matched pairs, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of 30-day respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence (10.7% vs 5.1%, relative risk [RR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.79-2.49).

Vaping-related disorder was also associated with increased risks of pneumonia (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.40-4.28), respiratory failure (RR 2.48, 95% CI 1.98-3.10), bronchospasm (RR 1.92, 95% CI, 1.38-2.68), and noninvasive ventilation (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.64-3.98).

Vaping-related disorder combined with cigarette nicotine dependence was associated with a higher risk of respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence alone (RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53), whereas vaping-related disorder alone showed a larger RR increase than neither diagnosis (RR 3.11, 95% CI 2.56-3.76).
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Useful for risk stratification and hypothesis generation, but avoid causal bedside changes unless supported by interventional evidence.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.title: Association of preoperative vaping-related disorder versus cigarette nicotine dependence with postoperative respiratory complications: a multicentre matched cohort study.
articles.summary: Among 3817 matched pairs, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of 30-day respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence (10.7% vs 5.1%, relative risk [RR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.79-2.49). Vaping-related disorder was also associated with increased risks of pneumonia (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.40-4.28), respiratory failure (RR 2.48, 95% CI 1.98-3.10), bronchospasm (RR 1.92, 95% CI, 1.38-2.68), and noninvasive ventilation (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.64-3.98). Vaping-related disorder combined with cigarette nicotine dependence was associated with a higher risk of respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence alone (RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53), whereas vaping-related disorder alone showed a larger RR increase than neither diagnosis (RR 3.11, 95% CI 2.56-3.76). Electronic cigarette aerosols may promote airway inflammation, bronchial hyperreactivity, and impaired mucociliary defence, but their perioperative respiratory safety remains uncertain. We examined whether preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence.
